summary: Stone County, MS tower on the De Soto National Forest, built by a CCC company in 1934 per NHLR, registered 2003, on standby for fire detection; height and cab sources disagree.

facts.design: 100-ft Aermotor LS-40 tower with metal cab per NHLR; a 1943 Coast and Geodetic Survey description gives 110 ft steel tower with glass-enclosed cab
facts.status_note: Register lists it on standby status for fire detection and as a radio relay site; standing in 2023 per Forest Lookouts list.

events.note: Constructed by a CCC company with enrollees from New Jersey (NHLR)
Biloxi Ranger District Lookout Club organizing meeting held at the tower (Biloxi Daily Herald, as quoted)
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description, reproduced on a National Geodetic Survey page: 110 ft steel tower with glass-enclosed cab
Listed as standing (Google Earth) on Forest Lookouts list

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved. NHLR gives 100 ft; the 1943 NGS description gives 110 ft. Both are reported in the story.
Not resolved. NHLR says metal cab; the 1943 NGS description says glass-enclosed cab. Both are reported in the story.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved date conflict: a Living New Deal page (https://livingnewdeal.org/sites/desoto-national-forest-airey-work-center-mchenry-ms/) says construction of the Airey Work Center began in 1935 under the CCC. The fetch returned 403, and the WebFetch paraphrase cannot be quote-checked, so the story does not use it. The NHLR 1934 date is used for the tower. A blog (https://thedirtymule.com/trails/desoto-national-forest-airey-lake-fire-tower-circuit/) also returned 403 and was not read. Access level not found in any source readable here, so it is omitted. Record change: the brief's record had no build event; 1934 added from NHLR.
